rv.q: The playwright and director Daniella Caggiano have done a surprisingly good job of managing all the moving parts within an overall logical framework.
The performances by Julia Lester, Zoe Dean, Mariyea and Sophie Zmorrod are riveting enough to supersede this dramaturgical problem.
Like costume designer Olivia Vaughn Hern’s corsets, Hungry Women has good bones.
A femme-forward depiction of rage and truth.
However, Maney and the play’s director, Daniella Caggiano, never quite settle on a tone, confusing the audience and undercutting the play’s deceptively straightforward message.
Though its ambitious triptych doesn't fully realize the promise of its premise, Hungry Women remains an imaginative, sharply written satire that refuses easy answers.

cn.t: Critics find this darkly comic "what if men went extinct" premise intriguing but unevenly executed, with strong performances from Julia Lester and Sophie Zmorrod unable to fully overcome a script that tries to juggle too many genres and themes at once.

vr.q: Hungry Women is going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation.
